why_this_point: dapo_n64_cap40_kv1_normal and kv0.6_normal both show 0 real preemptions, confirmed by direct measurement -- this point was found by testing util={0.50,0.40,0.35} in parallel and picking the first that actually breaks (0.40: 73 preemptions; 0.35: 87, confirming it is a real threshold not a single fluke)

root_cause_verified_via_source_probes.conclusion: num_blocks resolution is fresh and correctly utilization-sensitive (not stale); the preemption code path is real, reachable, and was exercised 576086 times; Frontier's pool genuinely filled to 100% capacity. The 0-preemption outcome is caused by Frontier's analytical non-KV-memory estimate reserving a roughly constant ~1900-2100 fewer blocks for non-KV use than real vLLM's actual allocation, which is a small fraction of the pool at util=0.9 (harmless) but a large fraction at util=0.4 (enough extra headroom to absorb all 73 of this workload's real preemptions, which sit close to vLLM's true capacity boundary)

root_cause_1_fixed.mechanism: Silent request-loss bug in VLLMv1EngineReplicaScheduler._schedule_waiting_requests (Phase 2 admission). Four skip branches exist for a waiting-queue-front request that can't be scheduled this iteration; three correctly do waiting_queue.popleft() + skipped_waiting_requests.append(request) + continue so the request is merged back into the real queues at the end of the function. The fourth (triggered when the per-batch token budget is already exhausted by earlier requests in the same pass, vllm_v1_engine_replica_scheduler.py:3384-3386 before the fix) did popleft()+continue WITHOUT the append -- the request fell out of every tracked collection (not running/waiting/preempted/completed) and was never revisited. Retroactively explains the kv0.5 point's unexplained 'completed_requests: 60/64' (same bug, 4 requests, far less budget exhaustion at that looser setting).
root_cause_1_fixed.evidence: request_metrics.csv for the unfixed run: the 25 missing requests (e.g. req 48) have blank request_e2e_time AND blank request_total_preemption_count -- never went through any tracked completion or preemption path. Their last ledger appearances are scattered across the whole 27.8s-249.75s range, not synchronized, consistent with being dropped whenever this specific branch fires rather than one global failure.
root_cause_1_fixed.fix_applied: Added the missing skipped_waiting_requests.append(request) call. 1 code line + 6-line comment, file: frontier/scheduler/replica_scheduler/vllm_v1_engine_replica_scheduler.py.
root_cause_1_fixed.verification: Re-ran kv0.5c with the fix. Requests no longer vanish -- but the run still does not complete; it now raises RuntimeError('Sequential simulation ended with non-empty scheduler state') at the same simulated time (249.76s) instead of silently writing a wrong result. Confirms the fix is correct (simulator.py's pre-existing safety check now fires because the scheduler state is no longer falsely empty) and surfaces root_cause_2 below.

root_cause_2_not_fixed.mechanism: A second, independent bug: nothing re-triggers a Phase 2 admission attempt when the running queue empties out while _preempted_requests still has pending work. The ledger's last 5 batches before the stall all contain only one request (req 20, whose own request_e2e_time of 249761ms matches the stall point exactly) -- the simulation halts the instant the last RUNNING request completes, even though other requests are sitting preempted and waiting to be retried.
root_cause_2_not_fixed.location: Not yet located precisely -- the actual ClusterScheduleEvent re-scheduling logic lives in frontier/scheduler/cluster_scheduler/base_cluster_scheduler.py (6000+ lines) and frontier/events/global_schedule_event.py, a separate subsystem from where root_cause_1 was found and fixed.
root_cause_2_not_fixed.status: Found and evidenced, not fixed -- a comparably-sized investigation to root_cause_1, not a small follow-on. Left as a precise, reproducible open problem.

dp_id_bug_fix.root_cause: self._dp_id is referenced at two sites (line ~1338 and the is_empty() diagnostic at line ~4705) but is never assigned in VLLMv1EngineReplicaScheduler or its parent BaseReplicaScheduler. Traced the correct source value: frontier/scheduler/utils/replica_schedulers.py constructs one scheduler instance per DP lane via `replica_local_id=dp_id` (line ~132) -- BaseReplicaScheduler.__init__ already stores this as self._replica_local_id (base_replica_scheduler.py:54) but upstream's new diagnostic logging code was written against a `_dp_id` name that was never aliased to it.
dp_id_bug_fix.vllm_package_version_hypothesis: REFUTED with direct evidence, not assumed. grep for '^import vllm'/'^from vllm' across vllm_v1_engine_replica_scheduler.py, base_replica_scheduler.py, and replica_schedulers.py returns zero matches. Frontier's 'vllm_v1' scheduler is a from-scratch pure-Python reimplementation of vLLM v1's scheduling algorithm -- it never imports or touches the installed vllm package at all in this code path (the real vllm package is only touched in frontier/profiling/attention/, a structurally separate module). This bug has nothing to do with which vllm version is installed; it is a plain missing-attribute bug in Frontier's own newly-added code.
dp_id_bug_fix.fix_applied: Added `self._dp_id = replica_local_id` in BaseReplicaScheduler.__init__ immediately after the existing `self._replica_local_id = replica_local_id` line, as a named alias to the same value (None for non-DP cluster types, the DP lane index otherwise).
dp_id_bug_fix.verification: Re-ran the exact kv0.5c frontier.main command against the merged codebase. The AttributeError is gone -- the run now proceeds past the point where it crashed before. It still does not complete, but for the pre-existing, already-documented root_cause_2 reason: it halts at simulation_time=240.92s with global_scheduler_is_empty=false, raising the same 'Sequential simulation ended with non-empty scheduler state' error. The log shows the exact same signature as the original (pre-merge) root_cause_2 finding: the last request to complete before the halt is req=20 (TOKEN-ROLLOUT-COMPLETE at 240.92s), matching the original investigation's finding that the simulation stops the instant the last RUNNING request finishes while other requests remain stuck in _preempted_requests, never re-admitted.
dp_id_bug_fix.bug_2_verdict: NOT fixed by PR #40/#38 despite their titles/scope being suggestive -- this is now a directly observed result (ran the actual simulation past the point where bug #2 would fire), not an inference from reading diffs. The 'plausible fix' framing from the merge task is superseded: root_cause_2 is confirmed still present in origin/main at commit 7df62a2.
